newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to $15 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to $15 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $15 per tonne lower on Thursday, in line with losses in London overnight, traders said.
London cocoa futures were lower in thin trading early Thursday, with LIFFE September down 12 stg at the midday break, to 1,035 stg, after ranging from 1,044 to 1,030 stg.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly lower, pressured by local and speculative liquidation. September fell $19 a tonne, to $1,576, after ranging from $1,591 to $1,570. December ended $18 lower, at $1,625, while the remaining months finished down $12 to $16.
Technically, traders said September would face strong support at $1,545, followed by $1,525. Resistance at $1,600, with the next level seen at $1,610.

Traders await the U.S. second quarter grind figures due out on Friday at 0845 EDT. Most analysts expected the U.S. second quarter grind to rise by 5 to 10 percent compared with the same year-ago period, although estimates ranged from a 5 percent decrease to a 15 percent increase.

In 1996, U.S. second quarter grindings rose by 4.85 percent to 82,713 tonnes against a revised 78,886 tonnes in the 1995 second quarter. In the first quarter of 1997, grindings surged 20.74 percent to 95,435 tonnes versus the same year-ago period.
